hero.kicker: Lawn care, landscaping and snow removal in Flint Township, MI
hero.title: Flat lawns, heavy soil, **clean stripes.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes looks after Flint Township yards all year: weekly mowing, spring and fall cleanups, bed rebuilds and shrub trimming, and driveways plowed by our own trucks in winter, with a free estimate to start.

about.title: Flint Township yards are older and **slow to drain.**
body: Flint Township wraps around the southwest side of the City of Flint, but it is its own government, run from the township hall on South Dye Road. Most homes here went up in the 1960s and 70s, so the lawns and foundation plantings have had fifty years or more to settle in, and to grow past where anyone meant them to.

The ground is mostly flat, heavy soil that drains slowly, and the low spots drain worse. Lawns stay soft into spring, water sits after a hard rain, and beds have to send water away from the foundation.

There is a big commercial side too. Retail lines Miller, Linden and Corunna Roads, offices sit along Beecher Road, and about a quarter of the homes are in apartment buildings of three or more units. We keep lots and grounds as well as houses.

points.title: Subdivision streets are plowed last
points.body: Township roads belong to the Genesee County Road Commission, or to MDOT for state roads. The county plows subdivision streets last, and clearing your own drive is a separate job that our [snow removal](/snow-removal-flint-township-mi/) covers.

points.title: Yard waste goes out on Thursdays
points.body: Emterra picks up compost weekly from April through November, on Thursday, in brown yard waste bags or marked cans. It does not take contractor generated material, so whatever our crew cuts or rakes, we haul away.

points.title: No burning leaves or clippings
points.body: The township fire department's open burning guidelines prohibit burning leaves, pine needles and grass clippings. A cleanup that hauls everything off is the simple way around that.

points.title: Shrubs at the end of the drive
points.body: The Road Commission says bushes, fences and other items near the right of way can block a driver's view at driveways and intersections. Keeping those shrubs trimmed low helps you and your neighbors see the road.

logistics.title: How we work in Flint Township.
body: Call or text Rob at [(810) 990-3040](tel:+18109903040), or use the [estimate form](/get-an-estimate/). He comes out, walks the property with you, suggests what it needs and quotes a price, at no charge.

The township is about 20 minutes from our shop on Embury Road in Grand Blanc. Mowing runs weekly on a set day, cleanups are timed to the weather and the ground, and winter service gets set up with Rob before the first snow.
Everything we cut, rake or dig leaves in our trailer, so your Thursday pickup stays free for your own bags.

faq.q: Do you work in Flint Township?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes does [lawn mowing](/lawn-mowing-flint-township-mi/), [spring cleanups](/spring-cleanup-flint-township-mi/), [fall leaf removal](/leaf-removal-flint-township-mi/), [landscaping](/landscaping-flint-township-mi/), [shrub trimming](/shrub-trimming-flint-township-mi/), [snow removal](/snow-removal-flint-township-mi/) and [commercial work](/commercial-snow-removal-flint-township-mi/) here. We are licensed and insured, and estimates are free.

faq.q: Is Flint Township the same as the City of Flint?
faq.a: No. Flint Township is a separate charter township that wraps around the southwest side of the city, with its own township hall, its own rules and its own trash hauler. Its roads are kept by the Genesee County Road Commission, while the city plows its own streets.

faq.q: Who plows the roads in Flint Township?
faq.a: The Genesee County Road Commission, except state roads, which MDOT maintains. The county does expressways and main roads first and subdivision streets last, and it says driveways getting plowed in by its trucks is unavoidable.

faq.q: Can I burn leaves in Flint Township?
faq.a: No. The township fire department's open burning guidelines prohibit burning leaves, pine needles and grass clippings. Leaves can go out for Emterra's weekly compost pickup in brown bags or marked cans, or we can vacuum them up and haul them away.
